description: Dario Amodei's stance on open-weight AI is questioned. Initially founded on safety, Anthropic now faces scrutiny over its evolving position on AI accessibility and government regulation. Is it self-serving? #OpenAI #Anthropic #AIDebate #AISafety #Tech

top_comments.author: @MountainDude-y5m
top_comments.text: Interesting argument, but I'd push back on the framing. Anthropic's pivot is predictable. Every lab eventually learns 'safety' maps suspiciously close to competitive incentives. The harder question: how do you constrain behavior after the weights are out?

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: Good point. After weights are out, you can’t control the model itself — only how it’s used. “Safety” ends up overlapping with competitive incentives pretty fast. Would you bet more on pre-release constraints or on runtime guardrails and policy after?

top_comments.author: @LogicPulse-v4l
top_comments.text: Left OpenAI over safety, now pushing for regulation that conveniently locks in Anthropic's market position.

top_reply.author: @STARTUPHAKK_sh
top_reply.text: Leaving over safety and then backing rules that raise costs looks strategic. It risks protecting users on paper while cementing advantage for those who can afford to comply. Can we design guardrails that don’t automatically favor the biggest labs?
